title: Multi-Account Containers: Complete Guide
description: Learn how to use Mozilla's Multi-Account Containers extension to separate your browsing experience into different color-coded tabs for better privacy and organization.
content:
Multi-Account Containers is an extension developed by Mozilla that allows you to separate your browsing experience into different color-coded tabs, to help protect your privacy. By using these containers, you can categorize your browsing based on purpose and create tabs for Work, Banking, Shopping and Personal browsing. For an extra layer of privacy, you can also integrate Mozilla VPN.

Pro Tip

Multi-Account Containers is especially useful for users who need to maintain separate browsing contexts for different purposes, such as work and personal activities, or for managing multiple accounts on the same website.

What you can do with Multi-Account Containers

Account Management

  • Sign in to multiple accounts on a single website (e.g. personal and work email accounts)
  • Manage different identities without conflicts
  • Keep shopping, banking, and social media accounts separate

Privacy Protection

  • Protect browsing with VPN integration
  • Prevent tracking and security attacks
  • Avoid social network footprints

Site Organization

  • Assign websites to containers automatically
  • Hide/Show and sort tabs by container
  • Create color-coded browsing environments

Cross-Device Sync

  • Sync containers across devices signed in with your Mozilla account
  • Carry over container names and site assignments
  • Maintain consistent organization everywhere

Installation Guide

1

Visit the Extension Page

Go to Firefox Multi-Account Containers on the Mozilla Add-ons website.

2

Add to Firefox

Click the Add to Firefox button on the extension page.

3

Confirm Installation

Click Add if you agree with the permissions requested by the extension.

Important Note

Containers are disabled in Private Browsing windows and when Never Remember History is selected in your privacy settings.

Opening Websites in Containers

1

Access Container Menu

Click the Containers icon in the toolbar (if you don't see it, click the extensions button in the toolbar, then click the containers icon).

2

Select Container

Choose the container you want to open from the dropdown menu.

Quick Tip

Right-click the new tab button to bring up the Containers menu for faster access.

Opening Bookmarks in Containers

To quickly open a bookmark in a container, you need to allow the extension to access your bookmarks:

1

Access Extension Settings

Click the menu button, go to Extensions and themes and select Extensions.

2

Configure Multi-Account Containers

Click Multi-Account Containers in the installed extension list.

3

Enable Bookmarks Access

Select Preferences and check Enable Bookmarks Menus.

After allowing access to your bookmarks, you can right-click any bookmark and select Open Bookmark in Container Tab.

Right-Click Menu Options

The right-click menu provides convenient ways to manage your Containers and control how links are opened:

Always Open in This Container

This checkbox allows you to specify that all links from the same website should open in the same Container.

Hide This Container

This option allows you to temporarily hide the current Container and all its tabs.

Move Tabs to a New Window

This option allows you to move all the tabs in the current Container to a new window.

Managing Your Containers

Create New Containers

  1. Click the Containers icon in the toolbar
  2. Click Manage Containers
  3. Click New container

Customize Containers

  1. Click the Containers icon in the toolbar
  2. Click Manage Containers
  3. Change color, icon, or name

Remove Containers

  1. Click the Containers icon in the toolbar
  2. Click Manage Containers
  3. Choose container to remove
  4. Click Delete this container

Managing Site Assignments

Always Open a Site in a Container

  1. Click the Containers icon in the toolbar
  2. Click Always open this site in…
  3. Select the container for the current site

Remove an Assigned Site

  1. Click the Containers icon in the toolbar
  2. Click Manage Containers
  3. Select the container with the assigned site
  4. Click Manage site list
  5. Hover over the site and click the trash icon

Limit to Designated Sites

You can restrict a container to only open sites assigned to it. Other sites will be opened in No Container.

  1. Click the Containers icon in the toolbar
  2. Click Manage Containers
  3. Select the desired container
  4. Enable Limit to designated sites

VPN Integration

You can keep your browsing data separate and stay protected with Multi-Account Containers. Additionally, you can integrate Mozilla VPN into each container to add an extra layer of protection to your container tabs. This way, you can have all the data from the containers pass through an encrypted tunnel using one of Mozilla's servers.

VPN Integration Benefits

  • Enhanced privacy protection for sensitive browsing
  • Geographic location flexibility for different containers
  • Additional encryption layer for container data
  • Separate VPN connections for different browsing contexts

To learn more about VPN integration, visit Protect your container tabs with Mozilla VPN.

Container vs. Profiles

It's important to understand the difference between containers and browser profiles:

FeatureContainersProfiles
Data SeparationCookies, sessions, storageComplete browser data
Setup ComplexitySimple, within same browserSeparate browser instances
Resource UsageLightweightHigher memory usage
Use CaseActivity separationComplete environment isolation

Common Questions

Are Firefox containers and Multi-account containers the same?

Firefox Containers and Multi-Account Containers are complementary features that help you keep your online activities organized. While both options allow you to separate your browsing into different container tabs, the Firefox Containers feature allows you to always open new tabs in containers.

On the other hand, Multi-Account Containers is an extension developed by Mozilla that fully optimizes Firefox containers and unlocks its full potential offering additional features, such as site assignments and integration with Mozilla VPN.

Note

These two features work together and you'll need to use both of them to make the most of all the features available.

How does this compare to the Facebook Container extension?

Facebook Container isolates Facebook and Facebook-owned sites automatically. The Firefox Multi-Account Containers is a more general extension that allows you to create containers and determine which sites open in each container. This extension can be customized to suit your needs for multiple sites and multiple logins, but takes more time to set up than Facebook Container.

You can use Multi-Account Containers to manually create a custom container for Facebook and assign facebook.com to it. However, unlike Facebook Container, Multi-Account Containers doesn't prevent you from opening non-Facebook sites in this custom container.

Can I use both Multi-Account Containers and Facebook Container?

Yes, but you need to be careful. Don't use Multi-Account Container to assign facebook.com to a container, and then try installing Facebook Container. If you are a Multi-Account Containers user and want to use both add-ons, unassign facebook.com, messenger.com, and instagram.com first, then install Facebook Container.

Privacy Benefits

Enhanced Privacy

Separate browsing contexts help maintain privacy and prevent cross-site tracking between different activities.

Better Organization

Organize your browsing by purpose and maintain clear separation between work, personal, and sensitive activities.

Important Note

This guide is based on Mozilla's Multi-Account Containers technology. For the most up-to-date information and official documentation, please visit the Mozilla Support page.
